title: EXP-07 Protocol Decisions: Scientific vs Engineering Classification
doctrine: Engineering implementation choices must NEVER silently determine scientific protocol values. Protocol decisions must be approved prior to implementation.

decisions.item: raw DN vs dB vs sigma0 (value domain)
decisions.rationale: Physical signal representation fundamentally affects gradient dynamics, backscatter interpretation, and physical validity. Cannot be decided by engineering convenience.
Normalization must reflect the physical value domain chosen; using unverified distribution parameters distorts radiometric features.
Whether the model predicts lookalike vs non-lookalike, 15-class segmentation, or hierarchical attribution is a core scientific question.
SAR sensor geometry (range/azimuth) implies non-isotropic speckle and directional physical features; arbitrary rotations can violate SAR physics.
Constrained by GPU memory and execution stability, though large-batch dynamics have secondary optimization effects.
Pure data loading throughput configuration; zero effect on scientific semantics or model weights.

decisions.item: neural architecture selection (e.g. UNet, ResNet, ViT)
decisions.rationale: Model inductive biases determine spatial feature extraction on SAR imagery; requires explicit experimental design.

decisions.item: loss formulation (BCE, Focal, Dice, weighted combo)
decisions.rationale: Directly governs severe class imbalance between background sea and sparse lookalikes; dictates penalty structure.
Learning rate schedule affects generalization and local minima traversal; learning stability is engineering-constrained.
Strict multi-seed evaluation is mandatory to ensure observed gains are statistically significant and reproducible.
Thresholds must be calibrated on DEV only and evaluated on HOLDOUT without tuning on holdout.
Best-epoch checkpointing criteria (metric choice) is scientific; disk storage format and frequency is engineering.
Implementing the PyTorch Dataset interface must follow the frozen scientific protocol without inventing protocol choices.
Tile sampling probabilities affect effective empirical risk minimization objective.
